Comment: Machine classes: 58 records in 10 categories and 5 tiers. Every number is a real-world class figure (mass, power, burn, price band); names are original. Adding a machine is a record plus a mesh recipe (Visual); category-specific numbers live in Specs and Curves.

vehicles.Comment: Small tracked groomer for cross-country trails: narrow gauge, light footprint, track-setter on the rear. 105 kW class.
Entry-level 150 kW piste machine, 3.5 m blade and 4.0 m tiller class. Slow on steep faces; fine for village hills.
The workhorse of the fleet: 260 kW, 12-way 4.3 m blade, 4.3 m tiller, 5-6 kPa ground pressure. Grooms a 40 m run in four lanes.
Terrain-park shaper with a 12-way park blade and a pipe-capable tiller; extra hydraulic flow for fine blade work.
390 kW class with the 6.0 m tiller: half the lanes of the mid-size cat on a wide run. Burns 40 L/h at work.
Mid-size chassis with a 4.5 t roof winch and 1,000 m rope: steep faces without spinning tracks. Needs a winch-cat licence.
Heavy chassis, 6.0 m tiller and a 4.5 t winch: the machine for black runs and the north face.
420 kW flagship with 6.0 m tiller and 5.0 m 12-way blade; highest work rate without a winch.
Diesel-electric drive: the engine runs at its sweet spot and burns about 20 % less; electric track motors give fine slow-speed control.
Flagship chassis with a 5 t winch and 1,200 m rope; the steepest terrain in the resort is groomable.
Battery-electric cat with a 400 kWh pack: 3-4 hours of grooming per charge, silent, recharged at the garage. Heavy from the pack.
Two-stage walk-behind for lift ramps and lodge decks: 10 kW gasoline, 35 t/h, 12 m throw.
Compact articulated blower for lots and cat tracks: 60 kW, 400 t/h, 20 m throw.
Two-stage blower on a 4x4 truck chassis: 200 kW to the drum, 1,200 t/h, clears a 2.4 m swath of the access road at 5 km/h.
Dedicated rotary blower with a 500 kW impeller engine: 3,500 t/h, 40 m throw. Opens the road after the big storm in one pass.
Airport-class 750 kW blower: 5,000 t/h, 45 m throw. Overkill for a village hill; a destination resort with a valley road needs it.

vehicles.Comment: Air/water lance on a wheeled sled, 6 m mast. Cheap and simple; needs compressor air (about 6 m3/min) and sits idle above -2 C.

vehicles.Comment: Wheeled fan gun with an 18 kW fan and onboard compressor; 45 m throw. The gun most resorts buy first.

vehicles.Comment: 10 m fixed lance on a hydrant pad: taller fall gives better snow at marginal temperatures; lowest energy per m3.

vehicles.Comment: Fan gun on a 4 m tower with a fixed hydrant: always where it is needed, out of the way of the groomers.

vehicles.Comment: Fan gun with weather station and automatic nozzle staging: starts itself the minute the wet-bulb allows and stops before it makes slush.

vehicles.Comment: 32 kW high-output fan gun: 90 m3/h at -8 C wet-bulb, 60 m throw. Drinks 110 L/min of water.
Plate-freezer snow factory: 9 m3/h of dense snow at any temperature from 400 kW of refrigeration. For the beginner area in a warm December.
40 kW compact tractor with a front plow and rear spreader: sidewalks, the lodge lot, the T-bar ramp.
90 kW utility tractor: the lot plow, the salt spreader and the trailer tug rolled into one.
Hydrostatic multi-tool carrier with a high-flow front hydraulic circuit: blower head, broom, plow or bucket on the front, spreader behind. Turns in its own length.
180 kW row-crop tractor: hauls the lowboy up the access road, runs a PTO blower, pushes a box plow.
300 kW articulated four-wheel-drive: tows the heaviest loads through unplowed snow, pushes the biggest box plow. Too big for the village.
Skid-steer with a snow bucket: lift ramps, lodge decks, loading the spreader. Spins in place.
Articulated compact loader, 1.0 m3 bucket: moves snow around the base, mounts a box pusher for the lot.
130 kW wheel loader with a 2.5 m3 snow bucket: loads dump trucks at the snow dump, hangs carriers with the forks.
Telehandler with 17 m reach: sets small towers, hangs carriers, lifts gun towers onto pads. Counts as a light crane.
200 kW loader with a 4 m3 light-material bucket: clears the lot in a fraction of the passes, feeds the snow factory, loads concrete aggregate.
Three-quarter-ton 4x4 pickup with a straight plow: the access road at 5 am, the parts run to town at noon.
4x4 service truck with a 2,000 L diesel tank, compressor, crane and a parts locker: the night shift's lifeline when a cat runs dry on the hill.
Single-axle 6 t dumper: hauls snow off the lots, aggregate to the batch plant, salt from the depot.
Tandem-axle 16 t dumper: the snow-haul workhorse and the concrete aggregate hauler for tower footings.
10,000 L diesel bowser on a 6x4 chassis: fills the depot cube in one trip and can top up a whole fleet in the field.
8 m3 transit mixer: tower footings need concrete on site within 90 minutes of batching, so the road must be open.
6x4 tractor with a 40 t lowboy trailer: moves groomers between resorts, brings the crawler crane and the tower sections up the road.
Single-axle plow truck with a 3.4 m V-plow and a 4 m3 salt hopper: the access road and both lots before the guests arrive.
Tandem plow truck with front plow and side wing (5.5 m cleared per pass) and a 7 m3 hopper: the valley road in one run each way.
8,000 L brine truck: anti-icing before the storm uses a third of the salt of spreading after it, and the lots stay black.
Motor grader with a 4.3 m moldboard: cuts packed snow and ice off the road, grades run corridors in the summer, shapes the lot berms.
Two-seat 4x4 utility vehicle with a cargo bed: mechanics, patrollers and parts around the base on plowed ground.
Wide-track utility sled with a hitch: tows the fuel sled, moves a mechanic to a dead cat, drags the trail roller.
Fast patrol sled: first on scene, sweeps the runs at close, carries the avalanche kit.
Side-by-side on four track kits: goes where the wheeled one bogs, carries two people and 300 kg of parts up the cat track.
Rescue sled with the toboggan hitch and heated grips: evacuation of an injured guest or a stranded operator in a whiteout.
2 t mini excavator: hydrant trenches, gun pads, the T-bar footings. Rides up on the light dump truck.
20 t crawler excavator: tower footings in one shift each, corridor clearing with the grapple, lifts a 3 t tower section in a pinch.
Crawler dozer: run grading in autumn, snow farming at the base in winter. Pushes what a groomer's blade cannot.
40 t all-terrain crane: sets chair and gondola towers within reach of the cat track. Needs a firm, near-level pad.
100 t lattice-boom crawler crane: gondola and 3S tower work where the terrain allows tracks. Arrives on three lowboys.
Walking (spider) excavator: legs and wheels articulate individually, so it digs footings on 45-degree faces the crawler cannot reach.
3,000 L double-walled diesel cube: extra depot storage with a dispensing pump. Delivered full.
Trailer-mounted 120 kW diesel pump: 30 L/s at 200 m head. Bridges a snowmaking line until the pump house is upgraded.
Trailer-mounted 150 kW compressor: 20 m3/min at 8 bar for a bank of lance guns.
